government.note: Parliamentary co-principality. The heads of state are jointly the two co-princes: the Bishop of Urgell (Episcopal Co-Prince, appointed by the Pope) and the President of France (Lay Co-Prince, ex officio). Each co-prince appoints a personal representative. The Head of Government (Cap de Govern) is chosen by the General Council.

holders.note: Coadjutor bishop from 12 July 2024; succeeded on 31 May 2025.

offices.note: Held ex officio by the Roman Catholic Bishop of Urgell, who is appointed by the Pope.

system.note: Parallel voting: 14 members by national-list proportional representation and two members for each of the seven parishes. seats_2000 is the 1997 election result: the Liberal Union won 10 seats and allied parish lists 6 (16 in total, under and.pla); the National Democratic Group (6), New Democracy (2), Democratic National Initiative (2) and the Lauredian Union list (2) are under 'others' because no founding dates were found for them.

chambers.review_note: Add party records (with founding dates) for the National Democratic Group, New Democracy and the Democratic National Initiative and move their 10 seats out of 'others'; confirm no changes between 1997 and 1 January 2000.

start_2000.ideology_support_note: Estimate from the 1997 national-list shares: Liberal Union 42.27% (liberal conservative); National Democratic Group 28.33% split evenly between Christian democrats (later the Democratic Party) and social democrats (later the PS); New Democracy 17.55% (social democrat, later the PS); Democratic National Initiative 11.85% (Christian democrat, later the Democratic Party). The splits are an estimate.
